title: Deadline-aware admission controller with inline partial-response
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: During cross-region failover and sustained spikes we observed tail latency and SLO violations driven by large generative requests that block priority lanes. Current shedding strategies either drop requests entirely or serve low-fidelity variants, but they lack a bounded-time guarantee for delivering a useful partial response back to clients.

Goal: Implement a deadline-aware admission controller that decides admission based on per-request deadline budgets and offers an inline partial-response pathway: instead of dropping, the runtime can accept a request with a shorter token budget or trigger an early finalize/summary flush so clients receive timely, useful output. The feature should integrate with existing priority queues, token-bucket reservations, and circuit-breaker signals.

Scope: Design + prototype server-side controller, small API additions to expose deadline/hint fields, a runtime execution mode for partial/early-finalize responses, and observability hooks (per-request decision label, tokens-served, partial vs full).

Why different: Most existing playbooks focus on binary admission or fidelity variant fallback. This ticket pairs admission decisions with an inline degradation mode that preserves request continuity (streaming partial outputs) and allows client libraries to surface progressive content while latency SLOs are met.

Artifacts: Confluence design (https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/DA-2026-deadline-admission), spike notes (internal drive link), and a prototype PR (below).

Related incident: Incident INC-2025-11-17-Failover documented that 30% of requests timed out when region us-west recovered; root cause section points to large chat sessions without deadline hints. This ticket targets a remediation path to reduce timed-out requests by enabling early useful responses.
acceptance_criteria: Controller honors per-request deadline header and drops/accepts based on computable remaining token-time budget
Accepted-with-degrade requests produce a partial-response stream that includes an explicit "partial=true" metadata frame and a finish_reason tag
SLO impact: under a synthetic 2x traffic spike test, P95 latency for priority tier reduces by at least 30% compared to current baseline with same dropped request rate
Metrics: new telemetry shows decision counts (accept, accept-with-degrade, reject), average tokens served for degraded requests, and broken-out SLO success by decision label
E2E tests: client SDK integration test that verifies partial stream behavior and fallback to full-run when deadline allows
notes: 2026-01-12: Spike/proof-of-concept run — local runtime prototype can trigger an early finalize and return summarized tokens; prototype uses greedy truncation + summary heuristics
2026-01-20: Design review with runtime and SDK teams. PMs asked for stable telemetry and opt-out per-customer flag. Design updated to include config per-tenant with default opt-in for P0 customers.

2026-01-28: Raised trade-off: partial responses may not be acceptable to some enterprise customers; added per-tenant policy and per-route opt-out and a clear Audit log entry when partial mode is used.

2026-02-02: Security review triage — no new data flows, but must record partial-response decision in audit logs for compliance. Marked security_review_required=false after review because no secrets are exfiltrated.
2026-02-10: Load test in staging (us-west/us-east multi-region failover simulation) shows 27% reduction in requests hitting circuit breaker thresholds when partial-response enabled
Design note: fallback priority lanes still honored — if accept-with-degrade would violate tenant throughput caps we reject instead of degrading
decisions: Expose optional per-request Deadline-Ms header and SDK helper wrappers
Implement accept-with-degrade path as a runtime execution mode producing explicit partial frames rather than opaque truncation
Per-tenant opt-out flag gated in control plane; default opt-in for self-serve customers
Telemetry must include decision label for downstream SLO attribution
next_steps: Complete PR for runtime greedy-early-finalize implementation (owner: Omar) — plan to land prototype behind feature flag
SDK team to add Deadline-Ms header helper and a partial-stream consumer sample
Staging perf run across us-west/us-east failover scenarios and collect decision-labeled metrics
Follow-up: stakeholder review with enterprise CS for opt-out policy and update Console UI to show per-tenant partial-mode usage
